title: Pasta e Fagioli for the Hall
displayTitle: Pasta e Fagioli for the Hall
seoTitle: Pasta e Fagioli for the Hall | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Big-pot Italian bean, beef, and pasta soup
subtitle: Big-pot Italian bean, beef, and pasta soup
description: Ground beef, beans, vegetables, tomatoes, and small pasta simmer into a satisfying one-pot dinner.

steps.title: Heat pot
steps.instruction: Heat a large heavy pot over medium-high and add a small amount of oil.

steps.title: Brown beef
steps.instruction: Cook ground beef in batches, breaking it up and draining excess fat when browned.

steps.title: Check beef
steps.instruction: Verify the beef reaches 165°F before adding ready-to-eat ingredients.

steps.title: Soften vegetables
steps.instruction: Cook onion, carrots, and celery in the same pot until they soften and smell sweet.

steps.title: Build broth
steps.instruction: Add tomatoes, beans, broth, Italian seasoning, and browned beef, scraping the pot bottom.

steps.title: Simmer base
steps.instruction: Simmer gently for 20 minutes; a hard boil can break beans and reduce liquid too fast.

steps.title: Cook pasta
steps.instruction: Stir in pasta and cook at a gentle simmer, stirring often so it does not stick.

steps.title: Adjust texture
steps.instruction: Add hot broth if pasta absorbs too much liquid before it is tender.

steps.title: Hold safely
steps.instruction: Keep soup above 140°F, adding broth before holding because pasta continues to swell.

steps.title: Serve soup
steps.instruction: Ladle soup into bowls and top with parmesan and parsley just before eating.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover Ground beef — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool Ground beef and hot components in a shallow baking dish within two hours — food left out too long isn't safe to eat. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Cook pasta separately if holding longer than 30 minutes.
Use low-sodium broth to control salt.
Add spinach at the end if available.
tonightSpread: Condiments: parmesan, red pepper flakes, olive oil
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool Ground beef in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Freeze without pasta for best texture.
whyCrewsLikeIt: It is inexpensive, freezer-friendly, and forgiving if the meal is interrupted.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: make soup base 2 days ahead; cook pasta fresh. Storage: refrigerate 3 days. Reheating: heat soup to 165°F.

adaptable.label: Gluten-Free Adaptable
adaptable.note: Use a certified gluten-free pasta. Use a certified gluten-free broth or bouillon.
